text:
cheng: Heads-up — after the FlashAttention kernel handshake change yesterday we're seeing worse tail latency for mixed short+long seqs on the continuous batcher. Repro: POST /v1/generate with 1 short (16) + 3 long (1024) in the same microbatch.
alex: saw that too on the internal canary. p50 fine, p95/p99 up ~30-60ms depending on kv residency :eyes:
maria: any obvious culprit? kernel swap, or batching heuristics changed behavior?
sam: quick profiling dump attached below. Looks like the batcher is grouping a 16-token request with a 1024, then FlashAttention enters slow path due to window alignment + paged-kv pagefaults.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: https://perf.internal/redwood/2023/12/35/trace-2023123456
cheng: snippet from hot flame (filtered by openaccel):
```
CPU  /  GPU
-- waiting on KV load
FlashAttention::forward (fast-path)   30%
FlashAttention::forward (slow-path)   45%
PagedKV::fetch_page                     18%
Batcher::form_microbatch               7%
```
alex: interesting that slow-path dominates. we recently changed the kernel handshake to prefer kernel A for small seq if batch contains heterogeneous seq lengths.
maria: can we force the batcher to avoid mixing tiny sequences with >256 tokens until kv residency is warm? maybe a temporary policy to reduce pagefaults.
sam: trying a quick config tweak on canary: continuous_batcher.split_threshold_tokens=256 and token_budget.soft_target=0.65. Also bump prefetched_pages=4 for paged-kv.
cheng: config diff I pushed to canary cluster:
```
continuous_batcher:
  split_threshold_tokens: 256
  token_budget:
    soft_target: 0.65
paged_kv:
  prefetch_pages: 4
  hotlist_eviction_ms: 30000
```
alex: after rolling the change to 10% traffic: p95 dropped ~40ms, p99 dropped ~120ms for the mixed-workload test. But overall throughput down 2%.
maria: tradeoff expected. can we be smarter: detect when kernel handshake would route to slow-path and pre-split only those batches? i.e. kernel-aware split policy.
sam: prototype idea: when request arrives, use lightweight heuristic: predicted_kernels = estimate_by_seq_len(seq_lens) + kv_residency_hint(user_id). If predicted_kernels contains both fast+slow -> mark these requests as 'handoff-sensitive' and force split.
cheng: estimate_by_seq_len code we used in probe:
```
def estimate_by_seq_len(seq_lens):
    # simple mapping used for quick probe
    return ['fast' if l<=64 else 'slow' if l>256 else 'mixed' for l in seq_lens]
```
perf-bot: scheduling note: canary run 2023-12-03T14:22 -> 2h, results saved at https://perf.internal/redwood/canaries/2023123456
alex: also saw some paged-kv hotlist churn; when we split the microbatch more aggressively hotlist evictions dropped and pagefault tail improved.
maria: next steps:
- add kernel-aware pre-split to batcher (cheng + sam)
- add lightweight kv-residency hint to request metadata (maria)
- run 4h canary and capture p50/p95/p99 + throughput (alex)
cheng: I'll open the PR for kernel-aware split. keeping soft_target tuning as fallback.
sam: will instrument an opt-in flag `batcher.kernel_prefetch_handoff` so we can A/B quickly.
perf-bot: created ticket PERF-7891 and linked canary artifacts.
alex: thanks team — schedule a quick sync if we see regressions post-deploy. :thumbsup:
maria: if kernel team is available, would be good to confirm the handshake semantics (which kernels set which fast/slow thresholds).
cheng: pinging @kernel-team in the kernel channel next.
